summary: Defines the initial version of the iana-if-type YANG module, which lists the types of network interfaces registered with IANA in a form usable by YANG-based management tools.

eli5.summary: There is an official list of kinds of network plugs. This document writes that list in a format that computer management tools can read directly.

questions: list of interface types in yang
what is the iana-if-type yang module
how are new interface types added to yang
subtitle: A machine-readable list of every IANA-registered network interface type, written as a YANG module.

tldr.problem: IANA keeps a registry of interface types (the ifType definitions), but YANG-based management had no matching module to refer to those types.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the iana-if-type YANG module, which has one identity per registered interface type, all based on the iana-interface-type identity, and tells IANA how to keep it in step with the registry.
tldr.outcome: The registry stays the single source of truth and IANA updates the module whenever a type is added; this RFC only defines the initial version.

today: RFC 7224 is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated. It defines only the initial version of the module; the text says the latest revision is obtained from the IANA web site.

sections.title: Purpose of the Module
sections.content:
This RFC defines the initial version of the iana-if-type YANG module, which holds interface type definitions. It reflects IANA's existing "ifType definitions" registry, in the same way that the IANAifType-MIB MIB module does.

The latest revision of the module can be obtained from the IANA web site. Whenever a new interface type is added to the registry, IANA updates both the IANAifType-MIB and the iana-if-type YANG module.
sections.eli5: The official list of connection types already existed. This document copies it into a new format, and the list keeper promises to keep both copies matching.

sections.title: How the Module Is Built
sections.content:
The module imports the interface-type identity from RFC 7223. It then defines iana-interface-type, an identity based on that one and used as the base for all interface types in the registry.

Each registered type is a separate identity statement that uses iana-interface-type as its base. Many carry a description and a reference to the RFC that defines the matching managed objects. The module's namespace is urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:iana-if-type and its prefix is ianaift.
sections.eli5: It is a family tree. There is one parent called interface type, and every kind of connection is a child hanging under it.

sections.title: Deprecated and Obsolete Types
sections.content:
The module keeps old types but marks their state. For example, ethernetCsmacd is for all Ethernet-like interfaces regardless of speed, as per RFC 3635. The identities iso88023Csmacd, starLan, fastEther and fastEtherFX carry status deprecated with a note to use ethernetCsmacd(6) instead.

Others, such as e1, frameRelayInterconnect and g703at2mb, carry status obsolete. The descriptions point to the replacement where one exists, for example the DS1-MIB.
sections.eli5: Old kinds of connection stay on the list, but with a sticker that says do not use this one, and which newer kind to pick instead.

sections.title: How IANA Keeps It Current
sections.content:
Interface types must not be added directly to the YANG module. They must be added to the "ifType definitions" registry, and then a new identity statement must be added to the module. The identity name is the same as the corresponding enumeration in the IANAifType-MIB.

Each identity should have a base of iana-interface-type, a status only if the registration is deprecated or obsolete, a description copied from the registry with lines no longer than 72 characters, and a reference copied from the registry plus the document title. Unassigned or reserved values are not in the module. Each update adds a new revision statement in front of the existing ones.

The RFC also registers the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:iana-if-type in the IETF XML registry and the module in the YANG Module Names registry. IANA added a note to the registry saying the module must be updated when it changes.
sections.eli5: The rule is: add new things to the main list first, then copy them into the machine-readable list in the same words and add a new version note.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that it does not introduce any technology or protocol, so there are no security issues to be considered for the document itself. It is a list of names that mirrors an existing registry.
sections.eli5: It is only a list of names, so there is nothing in it that a bad guy can attack.
